 Ohio State No. 1 in Big Ten Power Rankings | Indiana No. 4? Michigan No. 14?
 CBS Sports released its Big Ten Power Rankings on Thursday and there are some that will definitely surprise you. We have much more.
 Dave Biddle 12 It is no surprise that Ohio State is No. 1 in Robby Kalland's Big Ten Power Rankings on CBS Sports , but there are some eye-openers behind the Buckeyes. Personally, I would still have Indiana as the second-best team in the Big Ten, perhaps third, but UCLA gets the nod in the power rankings at No. 2. (And there is no doubt that the Bruins have been arguably the best feel-good story in all of college football this season. They're also undefeated and it is easy to make the argument for them at No. 2.)
 Then Northwestern gets the No. 3 spot, while the Hoosiers check in at No. 4. The Wildcats will travel to OSU for a game on Nov. 14. I'll be surprised if they stay ahead of Indiana -- who beat them earlier this year in Bloomington -- in these power rankings, but we'll see.
 The Buckeyes' opponent this week, USC, sits exactly in the middle of the conference at No. 9.
 Oregon is all the way down at No. 13, one spot ahead of No. 14 Michigan.
 Here is the full list, followed by some excerpts from the story:
 CBS SPORTS' BIG TEN POWER RANKINGS 
 1. Ohio State (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten)
 2. UCLA (7-0, 5-0)
 3. Northwestern (6-1, 3-1)
 4. Indiana (7-1, 4-1)
 5. Wisconsin (5-2, 3-1)
 6. Minnesota (5-2, 3-1)
 7. Iowa (5-2, 2-2)
 8. Nebraska (5-2, 2-2)
 9. USC (6-2, 3-2)
 10. Washington (4-3, 1-3)
 11. Purdue (3-4, 2-2)
 12. Illinois (4-3, 2-2)
 13. Oregon (4-3, 2-2)
 14. Michigan (4-3, 1-3)
 15. Rutgers (2-5, 1-3)
 16. Penn State (3-4, 0-4)
 17. Michigan State (2-6, 0-5)
 18. Maryland (2-5, 0-4)
 Here is what Kalland wrote about Ohio State:
 Ryan Day has kept his quarterback decision close to the vest this week between Luke Fahey (who came in as the backup against Indiana) and Tavien St. Clair . We'll find out Saturday who gets the start, whether Ohio State plays both QBs, and which QB can operate the Buckeyes' offense best against a USC defense that has been very friendly to opposing quarterbacks this season. The Ohio State defense can keep them in the mix for a title even with limited quarterback play, but Saturday is going to be telling of just how much this offense will slip in Julian Sayin's absence. 
 Here is what he wrote about USC, followed by Michigan:
 USC:
 Lincoln Riley's Trojans just cannot help but step on a few rakes during the Big Ten season. This time it was a road trip to Madison where Jayden Maiava struggled, the run game literally went backward, and the USC defense couldn't keep Wisconsin out of the end zone in the red zone. It's an all-too-familiar sight for USC fans, and while, at 6-2, the season's not over, the upcoming schedule is absolutely brutal. They get Ohio State at home this week, which is maybe the best time to get the Buckeyes in their first game without Julian Sayin, but they have two more top-10 teams in Indiana and UCLA left -- with a free space for the Maryland game in between. Riley desperately needs to go 9-3 to avoid real hot seat talk picking up this winter, and that's going to be an uphill climb with this defense. 
 Michigan:
 The good vibes around Tommy Carr lasted exactly one week before Indiana's defense brought a cold dose of reality. In spite of a rough outing from Carr, the Wolverines still had a chance late to beat the Hoosiers, and if it weren't for a catastrophic play-action call on the goal line (and a subsequent missed field goal), we might be talking about how Michigan's defense carried them to a stunning upset. That defense proved it's legitimately elite and can keep them in the game with most anyone. The problem is that Carr hasn't fixed the offense's problems, which clearly extend beyond Bryce Underwood . 
 Keep it locked to Bucknuts for full coverage of Ohio State football.
